turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi, how are you doing right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm training for a marathon and my calf has been feeling tight for three days.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Tightness can turn into an injury if you push through. Do you want to rest for a few days, or switch to easy cross training like cycling?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hold on, my friend and I need to figure something out. Wait until I'm back, okay?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Alex, quiz me. Bones of the arm. Go.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Okay, the long one from shoulder to elbow?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Correct. And the two in the forearm?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Radius and ulna. Which one's on the thumb side, though? I always mix them up.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Radius. Thumb, radius, think of a radio dial you turn with your thumb.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, that's good. Did you make that up?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Sorry, that took a while. I'm back.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sure thing. So, for your marathon calf, total rest or cross training?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Rest. I'd rather lose three days than three weeks.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Wise. Gentle stretching and foam rolling can help, then try a short easy run to test it.
